title: Ghost VRAM snapshot playbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal playbook + breadcrumbs for a recurring, intermittent GPU OOM that only shows up under our multi-worker inference harness (prefetch + shared mmap cache). Goal is to capture commands tried, minimal repro cues, odd error snippets, and hypotheses so I (or whoever inherits) don't repeat dead-ends.

Summary of the incident behavior:
- Symptoms: sudden allocation failures in the middle of a long-running inference stream. Model is a 13B LLM, pinned to single-GPU worker per process. The process dies with OOM, but nvidia-smi shows plenty of free VRAM (30% free).
- Unusual: other processes on same host can allocate and run; restarting the failing process fixes it temporarily. Problem surfaces after ~100k tokens and under sustained KV cache growth + small background host memory pressure.
- Suspected: library/driver ABI mismatch or stale kernel state that leads to failed CUDA context allocations or NVML reporting wrong free memory to runtime.

Commands and traces collected (chronological):
1) Base system checks (host):
  date; uname -a; cat /etc/lsb-release
  nvidia-smi -q | sed -n '1,80p'
  cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version || true
  # Output snippets:
  # NVIDIA-SMI 535.86.10    Driver Version: 535.86.10    CUDA Version: 12.1
  # NVRM version: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module 535.86.10 Thu Jul  4 18:09:44 UTC 2025

2) Container checks (inside failing container):
  ldd --version && ldd /usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | head -n 40
  ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so* || ls -l /usr/local/nvidia/lib64/libcuda.so*
  # Found: libcuda.so.1 -> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.535.86.10 (container shows same symlink)

3) Repro attempt with minimal runner: (script trimmed)
  ENV: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0; python repro_minimal.py --batch 1 --stream 100000
  # repro_minimal runs model, appends tokens in loop until OOM
  # Observed error (stderr):
  # RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 256.00 MiB (GPU 0; 47.90 GiB total capacity; 39.21 GiB already allocated; 128.00 MiB free; 1.23 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
  # But nvidia-smi at same timestamp: 12.3 GiB used, 35.6 GiB free.

4) NVML introspection (when process is alive):
  python -c "import pynvml; pynvml.nvmlInit(); h=pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex(0); print(pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo(h));"
  # Returns: total=51539607552, free=13107200000, used=38432407552  (matches nvidia-smi)

5) When the crash occurs, collected kernel logs:
  dmesg -T | tail -n 200 | sed -n '1,120p'
  # Example lines seen: 'NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=11453, Name: python, GPU has fallen off the bus.' (rare)
  # More common: 'NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed!' followed by 'NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.'

6) Driver/library mismatch errors occasionally interleaved (rare):
  # stderr snippet when observed during a restart:
  # nvidia-container-cli: initialization error: NVML: Driver/library version mismatch
  # WARNING: Unable to load libnvidia-ml.so.1: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1: version 'NVIDIA-ML-535' not found (required by /opt/runtime/lib/libnvidia-container.so.1)

What I tried so far and why (notes):
- Reduce batch size / force torch.cuda.empty_cache() periodically: temporary reprieve but not root cause. Useful as mitigation in production.
- Set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 (and 64): reduces fragmentation in some runs, but still OOM after long tail.
- Disable worker-level mmap cache (our prefetcher uses shared mmap): toggling it seems to change failure rate — plausible leak in mmap bookkeeping or race between processes attaching to same GPU buffer.
- Restarting nvidia-persistenced between runs: sometimes clears mystery state and makes runs stable for hours. That points at driver state.
- Tried LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 inside container: in one host this produced immediate 'version not found' messages. Reverted.
- Rolled forward host driver 525 -> 535 on a test rack (matching container libcuda): reduced frequency of OOM by ~70% in 48h stress, but did not eliminate.
- Run with MPS disabled/enabled: MPS didn't change frequency.
- Strace attach during allocation failure: lots of ioctl calls to device, then ENOMEM from some mmap calls in the runtime. Hard to interpret.

Additional diagnostic captures to gather next time (planned):
- On crash, capture: pmap -x <pid of python>, /proc/<pid>/maps, /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup to see host-side mappings.
- Use nvprof / CUPTI trace of kernel launches leading up to crash to check for kernel launch failures flagged by CUDA runtime.
- Use a small C repro that repeatedly cuCtxCreate/cuMemAlloc/free to see whether raw CUDA API fails when Python runtime shows OOM. This isolates PyTorch caching layer.
- Capture strace -f -tt -o /tmp/trace.<pid>.log for the process; capture ioctls to /dev/nvidiactl and /dev/nvidia0 around the failure.
- When failure occurs, do readelf -s on libcuda.so included in container vs host to check symbol versions.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Stale kernel/driver state (most likely) — long-lived processes + repeated context create/free leads to NV driver internal fragmentation or leaked resources; nvidia-persistenced restart temporarily recovers. Rationale: restart often helps and driver logs sometimes show RmInitAdapter failures.
2) Subtle ABI mismatch across host/container libs — some calls to libnvidia-container/libnvidia-ml expect specific symbol versions. When container image and host driver mismatch slightly (different minor releases), some calls fail sporadically and cause incorrect free accounting. Rationale: we saw the "Driver/library version mismatch" once after LD_PRELOAD fiddling.
3) PyTorch caching bug combined with mmap-backed shared KV cache — double-free or stale pointer in shared memory region causing allocator to think memory is consumed when it's not. Rationale: turning off mmap cache changes failure rate.
4) Real VRAM leak in the model (less likely) — but still possible when attention caching logic is buggy for certain prompt patterns. Rationale: repro script sometimes shows consistent leak when running specific token sequences.

Immediate mitigations for prod rollout (low friction):
- Add an auto-restart supervisor for processes that hit OOM (in Dedicated tier); add jittered backoff to allow nvidia-persistenced on host to settle.
- Expose PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF tuning (max_split_size_mb) flag in the runtime template.
- During scheduled low-impact windows, align container libcuda symlink to host driver version on a canary rack; monitor.

Longer-term actions and owners:
- (Infra) Add a nightly script to collect /proc/driver/nvidia and roll NVRM logs across fleet (Owner: Marco R.).
- (Runtime) Add an instrumentation probe that emits per-process CUDA context count and cached-allocation sizes every minute to metrics (Owner: Evelyn C.).
- (Research) Build minimal C repro to stress cuCtxCreate/cuMemAlloc/free and open a kernel-level bug with NVIDIA if reproducible (Owner: Aisha P.).

Unresolved questions / TODOs (for future runs):
- Does the problem correlate with kernel updates (check apt history on hosts that saw failures)?
- Can we instrument NVML to track per-process allocation vs PyTorch internal allocator snapshot (are we double-counting)?
- Is there any correlation with hugepages/transparent hugepages on the host? (we haven't toggled THP).

Useful one-liners to run during incident:
- tail -n 200 /var/log/nvidia-installer.log || true
- journalctl -k --since "1 hour ago" | grep -i nvrm || true
- python -c 'import gc,torch; gc.collect(); print(torch.cuda.memory_summary())'
- for p in $(pgrep -f python); do echo $p; pmap -x $p | head -n 40; done

Final notes:
- This doc is a scratchpad: if you pick it up, start by checking when the last nvidia-persistenced restart happened and correlate with job start times. Collect the pmap + NVML snapshot the next time this happens.
- Add any new error snippets here (grepable) so we can build a small regexp classifier in infra to auto-tag machines likely to need driver attention.

---
Changelog:
- 2025-11-08 initial capture (Aisha)
- 2026-01-15 added nvml and dmesg snippets after second rack failure (Marco)
- 2026-02-28 added hypotheses ranking and pragmatics for mitigations (Aisha)
